It has been an exceptionally volatile earnings season:

Information Technology stocks fell -1.2% on average in October on the first trading day after reporting earnings, the weakest performance among all sectors.

This was followed by Energy and Consumer Staples, with average 1-day returns of -0.3% and -0.2%, respectively.

On the other hand, 8 out of 11 sectors recorded positive 1-day performance after reporting earnings over the same period.

Consumer Discretionary benefited the most, at +1.9%, followed by Healthcare and Industrials at +1.5% and +1.2%, respectively.

As a result, the average stock gained +0.6% on the first trading day after reporting earnings.

Tech is deviating from the rest of the market.

Last Tuesday at 9:14am I opened a leveraged position because a friend had been in the same size since Monday night.

I assumed the move still had room because he was still holding.

By 2:47pm the reverse had already started.

By 6:03pm I was staring at a liquidation price I never planned to see.

Same asset. Same multiple.

The only difference was that I entered after the room had already been taken.

That is the cost of sizing by someone else’s position instead of by the asset’s own burn.

🚨📈 RELIANCE POSTS A RECORD-BREAKING Q2 FY27 PERFORMANCE!

Reliance Industries reported an exceptional quarter, with revenue jumping 27.8% to an all-time high of ₹3,62,268 crore. EBITDA also touched a record ₹62,409 crore, while net profit surged 33.8% to ₹29,550 crore.

The O2C business was a major contributor, delivering an operating profit of ₹25,203 crore, up 67.9%, backed by exceptionally strong refining margins amid global market disruptions. That's over ₹270 crore in operating profit every single day from energy operations alone!

Reliance also maintained a strong investment pace, spending ₹415 crore on capex every day, while bringing net debt down to ₹1,17,140 crore and keeping its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio at just 0.47x.

Record revenue, higher profitability, sustained investments and lower leverage — Reliance's Q2 numbers reflect the sheer scale of its business operations.
